description: Japchae Sweet Potato Glass Noodles is a beloved Korean dish featuring chewy glass noodles stir-fried with a colorful array of fresh vegetables and savory marinated beef. This vibrant and flavorful pasta is a staple for celebrations and everyday meals alike, offering a delightful balance of sweet and savory notes in every bite. It is a true culinary delight that showcases the best of Korean home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare the Noodles and Marinade the Beef
instructions.text: Boil a large pot of water and cook the sweet potato glass noodles according to package instructions, typically 6-8 minutes, until tender but chewy. Drain thoroughly, rinse with cold water to prevent sticking, then drain again and cut into shorter lengths with kitchen shears. In a bowl, combine sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 clove minced garlic, and black pepper. Mix well and let marinate for at least 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare and Blanch the Spinach
instructions.text: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Blanch the fresh spinach for about 30 seconds until wilted. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking, then squeeze out excess water. Season the blanched spinach with 1/2 tsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp sesame oil. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté the Vegetables Separately
instructions.text: Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Sauté the julienned carrots for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender. Remove and set aside. Repeat with sliced onions, cooking until translucent, then remove. Repeat with sliced rehydrated shiitake mushrooms, cooking until fragrant, then remove. Finally, quickly sauté the julienned red bell pepper for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened, then remove and set aside. Cooking vegetables separately helps maintain their distinct flavors and textures.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Beef
instructions.text: Add 1 tsp vegetable oil to the same pan. Add the marinated beef and stir-fry over medium-high heat until fully cooked through and browned, about 3-4 minutes. Break up any clumps. Remove the cooked beef from the pan and set aside with the vegetables.

instructions.title: Combine and Season the Noodles
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, add the cooked and drained glass noodles. Prepare the Japchae sauce by combining 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp sesame oil, and 2 cloves minced garlic. Pour the sauce over the noodles and mix thoroughly with your hands, ensuring the noodles are evenly coated and seasoned. The warmth of the noodles will help them absorb the sauce better.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Add all the sautéed vegetables (carrot, onion, mushrooms, bell pepper, spinach) and the cooked beef to the bowl with the seasoned noodles. Gently mix everything together until all ingredients are well combined and distributed. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, adding more soy sauce or sugar to your preference. Transfer the Japchae to a serving platter and garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Always cook vegetables separately to retain their distinct textures and colors; combining them too early can lead to overcooking and a muddy appearance.
For a vegetarian version, substitute beef with extra shiitake mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, or firm tofu, marinating them in the same sauce.
Japchae is delicious served warm or at room temperature, making it a perfect dish for potlucks or as a make-ahead side. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
